I am looking for a new mouse, but Logitech has a problem with cable coming loose and dicsconnecting/reconnecting mouse. They use the same system for all their mouses, so I will try to avoid them.

What are alternatives to Logitech G502 mouse?

Not sure if it suits your needs as it's not quite clear what features in particular you're looking for in a mouse outside of a sturdier cable, but have a look at the RedDragonite M 901 Perdition.

It's inexpensive and I'm completely satisfied with mine. Tons of buttons with good placement, the wave pattern on the num pad makes locating where your thumb is easy to do, up to 16400 DPI, and it has seven weights you can use to adjust the heft. Very well built and the scroll wheel is rubberized, large, and sturdy.

Good software too, profile switching, every button is programmable, and it does macros.

I used to have a Razer Naga Molten Edition mouse similar to my Perdition and I like this one a lot more. Really high quality for the money in fact. I bought it as a cheap temporary replacement for my Naga after the scroll wheel broke on it, and ended up liking it a lot more. I've had it for about 4 years now and it hasn't given me any problems.

I use a corsair M65. It feels nice and has a really long cable and I haven't had any problems with it. It doesn't have a ton of buttons on the side (forward, back and a thumb button) You can change the DPI to five different settings in the software which you can change with a set of buttons on the top of the mouse. I find I only use two different settings but it's nice to have.
